Placement volatility and alert complexity

Source: vignettes/placement-and-alerts.Rmd
placement-and-alerts.Rmd

How often a person in custody is moved within a year, how many alerts a record carries, and what follows from both.

Each section is one help page: what the function is for, the example of its help page as it runs, and the plot of its result where the package draws one. ?name gives the arguments and the value in full.

Placement volatility of each person-year

plcvol(): Counts how often a person’s placement region changes within a period (a fiscal year), from records that each carry the region at the time of placement ra and the region of the most recent placement rb. For a person-year with records r = 1, …, R in a given order the count is

ra <- c("East", "East", "West", "North", "North")
rb <- c("East", "West", "West", "North", "East")
plcvol(ra, rb, id = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2))
#> plcvol: 2 person-years, records in region order; mean volatility 1.5 (within 1, across 0.5)
#>  id n within across vm
#>   1 3      1      1  2
#>   2 2      1      0  1
plcvol(ra, rb, id = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2), ord = "given")
#> plcvol: 2 person-years, records in given order; mean volatility 1.5 (within 1, across 0.5)
#>  id n within across vm
#>   1 3      1      1  2
#>   2 2      1      0  1

Alert complexity of each person-year

alrtcx(): Counts the distinct alert configurations among a person-year’s records. Each record carries flags (in Ontario’s records the mental health, suicide risk and suicide watch alerts); its configuration is the tuple of the flags, (1, 0, 0) for a mental health alert alone, coded as the text "100". Alert complexity is the number of distinct configurations the person-year’s records span, and cx, complexity of two or more, is the treatment of Ruhela (2026, Appendix H).

f <- data.frame(mh = c("Yes", "No", "No", "Yes"),
                sr = c("No", "No", "Yes", "Yes"),
                sw = c("No", "No", "No", "Yes"))
alrtcx(f, id = c(1, 1, 2, 3))
#> alrtcx: 3 person-years; 1 (33.3%) span two or more alert configurations
#>  id n ac cx anyal
#>   1 2  2  1     1
#>   2 1  1  0     1
#>   3 1  1  0     1

Person-year table of a restrictive confinement release

otpyr(): Reduces a placement-level release of Ontario’s restrictive confinement records (table a01 of the open data, one row per person, fiscal year, pair of regions and alert configuration, with a count of placements) to one row per person and fiscal year, carrying placement volatility (plcvol()), alert complexity (alrtcx()) and the covariates of Ruhela (2026): gender, age group, fiscal year and regional cluster (the regions the person-year’s records name, sorted and joined by " + ").

d <- data.frame(
  EndFiscalYear = c(2025, 2025, 2025, 2026, 2026),
  UniqueIndividual_ID = c("a", "a", "b", "a", "c"),
  Region_AtTimeOfPlacement = c("East", "West", "East", "North", "East"),
  Region_MostRecentPlacement = c("East", "West", "East", "East", "East"),
  Gender = "Male", Age_Category = "25 to 49",
  MentalHealth_Alert = c("Yes", "No", "No", "No", "Yes"),
  SuicideRisk_Alert = "No", SuicideWatch_Alert = "No",
  Number_Of_Placements = c(3, 1, 2, 4, 1)
)
otpyr(d)
#> otpyr: 4 person-years, fiscal years 2025-2026 (2)
#>  year py  cx  vm
#>  2025  2 0.5 0.5
#>  2026  2 0.0 0.5

Count regression with a random intercept per cluster

cntmix(): Fits the log-linear model of a count with a normal random intercept for each cluster, log E[y_ij | u_j] = x_ij’ beta + u_j, u_j ~ N(0, sigma^2), with a Poisson or a negative binomial (variance mu + mu^2 / theta) response, by maximum likelihood with the Laplace approximation of each cluster’s integral (Breslow and Clayton 1993), as ‘glmmTMB’ and ‘lme4’ fit it. It is the main model of Ruhela (2026): placement volatility on alert complexity with a random intercept per regional cluster.

set.seed(2)
g <- rep(1:12, each = 40)
d <- rbinom(480, 1, 0.3)
y <- rpois(480, exp(-1 + 0.4 * d + rnorm(12, 0, 0.5)[g]))
cntmix(y, data.frame(d = d), g, fam = "poisson")
#> cntmix: poisson counts with a random intercept per cluster
#> 480 counts in 12 clusters; sigma 0.5101; log-likelihood -459.3308
#>         term     est     se      z         p    irr     lo    hi
#>  (Intercept) -0.8465 0.1695 -4.994 5.919e-07 0.4289 0.3077 0.598
#>            d  0.4339 0.1215  3.573 3.535e-04 1.5433 1.2164 1.958

Alert complexity and placement volatility, pooled or by fiscal year

cxvol(): The analysis of Ruhela (2026) on any release of Ontario’s restrictive confinement records: from the person-year table (otpyr()) it gives, for the years pooled or for each fiscal year, the share of person-years with complex alert profiles (cx = 1), mean placement volatility by group, the crude Poisson rate ratio (the ratio of the two means, infinite when every count without complex alerts is 0), the one-to-one nearest-neighbour propensity matching without replacement of each complex person-year to a control on age group, gender and fiscal year (cbatt(), in ‘MatchIt’’s default order), the count model on the matched frame with a random intercept per regional cluster (cntmix()), and the bounds on the average effect on the matched frame with no assumption and under monotone treatment response and selection (mtrbnd()).

set.seed(4)
n <- 600
p <- data.frame(year = sample(2025:2026, n, TRUE),
                gender = sample(c("Male", "Female"), n, TRUE, c(9, 1)),
                age = sample(c("18 to 24", "25 to 49", "50+"), n, TRUE),
                rc = sample(c("A", "B", "A + B", "C"), n, TRUE),
                cx = rbinom(n, 1, 0.2))
p$vm <- rpois(n, exp(-2 + 0.3 * p$cx + (p$rc == "A + B")))
cxvol(p, fam = "poisson")
#> cxvol: alert complexity (cx) and placement volatility (vm), years pooled
#>     sample   n     cx    vm1    vm0 crude matched    irr     lo    hi     p    bound
#>  2025-2026 600 0.1917 0.2174 0.2062 1.054     230 0.8477 0.5012 1.434 0.538 -0.06087
#> irr: rate ratio of the matched count model (poisson); bound: upper end of [0, bound] under monotone response and
#> selection (below 0, the data contradict the two assumptions)

Double machine learning of the effect of alert complexity

cxdml(): The interactive regression model of Chernozhukov et al. (2018) for the effect of complex alert profiles (cx) on placement volatility (vm) on the person-year table, by dmlx(): random forests (or another learner of dmlx()) for the outcome regressions and the propensity, nfold-fold cross-fitting, propensities kept within trim of 0 and 1, covariates gender, age group, regional cluster and (pooled, with yterm) fiscal year. Both the average effect (ATE) and the effect on the treated (ATTE) are given, from one set of cross-fitted nuisances. The same refusals as cxvol() apply.

set.seed(5)
n <- 400
p <- data.frame(year = sample(2025:2026, n, TRUE),
                gender = sample(c("Male", "Female"), n, TRUE),
                age = sample(c("18 to 24", "25 to 49"), n, TRUE),
                rc = sample(c("A", "B"), n, TRUE), cx = rbinom(n, 1, 0.3))
p$vm <- rpois(n, exp(-1.5 + 0.4 * p$cx))
cxdml(p, lrn = "glm")
#> cxdml: interactive model, effect of cx on vm (additive scale)
#>     sample   n estimand    est      se      lo     hi
#>  2025-2026 400      ATE 0.1571 0.06122 0.03713 0.2771
#>  2025-2026 400     ATTE 0.1336 0.05927 0.01742 0.2498

Placement volatility events by fiscal year

cxyoy(): The year-over-year table of placement volatility (Ruhela 2026, Appendix E, Table E15) from the person-year table: for each fiscal year the regional changes (vm summed), placements, person-years, the rates of changes per 1,000 placements and per 1,000 person-years with exact Poisson intervals, each year’s share of all changes, and the percent changes from the previous year of the count and of both rates. The rate intervals are qgamma(a/2, n) to qgamma(1 - a/2, n + 1) over the exposure, so a count of 0 has lower limit 0.

p <- data.frame(year = rep(2024:2026, c(50, 60, 70)), vm = rpois(180, 0.2),
                np = rpois(180, 20) + 1)
cxyoy(p)
#> cxyoy: regional changes per fiscal year
#>  year vm   np py   rnp rnplo rnphi   rpy rpylo rpyhi  share    dvm   drnp   drpy
#>  2024 12 1045 50 11.48 5.934 20.06 240.0 124.0 419.2 0.2667     NA     NA     NA
#>  2025 17 1245 60 13.65 7.954 21.86 283.3 165.1 453.6 0.3778 41.667  18.91  18.06
#>  2026 16 1467 70 10.91 6.234 17.71 228.6 130.6 371.2 0.3556 -5.882 -20.13 -19.33

Simulation of the alert complexity estimators

cxsim(): Draws person-year tables from the model of Ruhela (2026) and reports the bias, spread and interval coverage of the estimators of cxvol(). Each table has n person-years in ncl regional clusters with normal intercepts (standard deviation sdcl), an age group (three levels) and a gender, a treatment drawn from a logistic model in which the covariates and the cluster raise the chance of a complex profile, and a negative binomial count (dispersion theta) whose log mean is b0 + beta * cx plus the covariates and the cluster. With conf the person-year also has an unobserved trait that raises both the chance of treatment and the count (by conf on the logit and on the log mean): ignorability given the observed covariates then fails.

cxsim(reps = 1, n = 100, ncl = 5, b0 = 0, seed = 1)
#> cxsim: 1 tables of 100 person-years, log rate ratio 0.2624
#>      est   bias sd   rmse cover ok
#>    crude 0.4090 NA 0.4090    NA  1
#>    mixed 0.1381 NA 0.1381     1  1
#>  matched 0.0113 NA 0.0113     1  1
